title: Ночевка в подъезде  (Sleeping in the Hallway)

segments.t: Victoria tells Max they should wait before living together, leaving him alone in the hallway. Soon after, Kostya calls Max to ask him to return to their apartment. Let us listen to their conversation in Russian first.
Now let us examine the conversation line by line.
'Therefore I will not pressure you.' The little negative word sits right in front of the verb for 'will be', just like 'not' in English.
'Let everything remain as it was.' The question word for 'how' comes right at the start, followed directly by 'was'.
'Yes, but I...' Russian omits the present-tense verb 'to be' here, linking 'yes' directly with 'but', combining 'yes' with 'but' and 'I'.
'We will definitely live together.' Vika expresses this naturally by combining the word for 'surely' with 'will' and 'to live'.
'And now good night.' Russian omits the present-tense verb 'to be' here, linking 'now' directly with 'good', combining 'now' with 'good' and 'night'.
'Until tomorrow, Max.' Max delivers a punchy one-word reaction built around the Russian word meaning 'tomorrow'.
'Until tomorrow.' Vika delivers a punchy one-word reaction built around the Russian word meaning 'tomorrow'.
'Moved to live in the hallway.' Max uses the action verb meaning 'to move' to focus on the single completed result, pairing it with 'to live' and 'entrance'.
'Hi, Max.' Kostya delivers a punchy one-word reaction built around the Russian word meaning 'hi'.
'What do you need?' Russian builds this impersonally with the matching word ending ('to me' or 'to you') and 'it is necessary'.
'Max, come back.' — Notice the proper name meaning 'Max' paired with the verb for 'return'.
'We miss you.' Kostya delivers a punchy one-word reaction built around the Russian word meaning 'grabs'.
'We will divide the apartment by three.' Notice how naturally this everyday Russian phrase expresses the speaker's point.
'I will try to come.' Notice the self-directed ending on the verb for 'to try', which directs the action back onto the subject. Now let's listen to the whole conversation again from start to finish.

Victoria tells Max they should wait before living together, leaving him alone in the hallway. Soon after, Kostya calls Max to ask him to return to their apartment. Next time you watch the episode, listen for the Russian expressions for 'that's why' and 'to be' — you will catch every word right away. See you next time!

lines.fragment: Пусть остается все как было, всему свое время.
Переехал жить своей девушке в подъезд.
Ну, Костян, обещать не буду, но постараюсь.
